title: Asia's Cleanest Village Bans Sunday Tourists
paragraphs: Mawlynnong is a small village in the state of Meghalaya, in northeast India. Only a few hundred people live there. However, the village is famous across the country, and it receives many visitors. Now, the village has decided to stop day tourists from visiting on Sundays.

Mawlynnong became famous in 2003, when a travel magazine called it the cleanest village in Asia. In 2015, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi also praised the village in a radio address. Since then, more and more tourists have come to see it. According to the village committee, up to 1,000 tourists can visit in a single day during busy periods.

Keeping the village clean is part of daily life. Every Saturday, people in the village clean the streets together, and the village pays about 25 people to clean and look after gardens. Children learn about cleanliness at church and school. People who spit in the street can be fined about $10.

Tourism has changed the village. Many people have stopped farming and now work in tourism. There are now about 40 guesthouses and six restaurants. But the crowds also made life difficult for people in the village.

So, in January 2026, the village council decided that day tourists cannot visit on Sundays. Most people in the village are Christian, and they want time to go to church and rest. However, tourists who are staying overnight in guesthouses can still stay on Sunday. A guard at the village gate turns away other visitors.

Precious Khongdup, a member of the village committee who also runs a guesthouse, said, "We have to have a break." Khongdup added, "If we work the whole week, we don't have time for our children." One visitor from New Delhi who was turned away on a Sunday understood the decision. "They also need some time," the visitor said.
